# odyssey-008 (2.321–434) — new fixed renderings

Format matches conventions.md's fixed table: Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| διογενής (of Odysseus, 352, 366) | "Zeus-sprung" | "Zeus-born" | "godlike" (reserved for ἀντίθεος), "heavenly" (reserved for δῖος), "divine" (reserved for θεῖος), "godlike in form" (reserved for θεοειδής) |
| ἱερὴ ἲς Τηλεμάχοιο (409) | "the sacred force of Telemachus" | "the strong, sacred figure of Telemachus" | naturalising it to a bare epithet-plus-name ("mighty Telemachus"), which would erase the periphrasis Homer uses in place of the bare name — the same device as βίη Ἡρακληείη for Heracles |
| ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖς αἰειγενέτῃσιν (432) | "the immortal gods who are forever-born" | "the immortal, everlasting gods" | folding it into the already-fixed θεοὶ αἰὲν ἐόντες "the gods who are forever" — that formula is built on ἐόντες 'being', this one on γίγνομαι 'be born', and the two are kept as distinct literal renderings |
| ἔνθ’ αὖτ’ ἄλλ’ ἐνόησε θεά, γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη (whole-line formula, 382 = 393 within this part) | "Then again another thing devised the goddess, gleaming-eyed Athena." | "Then, in her turn, the goddess, gleaming-eyed Athena, thought of something else." | "conceived a new plan" (loses the plain sense of ἄλλο "another thing," not specifically a "plan"), "had another idea" (too casual for the register) |

## Notes on epithets extended to a new referent (no new row needed — the fixed rendering already covers the word itself)

- **ἐυκνήμιδες** (already fixed as "well-greaved" for ἐυκνήμιδες Ἀχαιοί) is applied at 402 to ἑταῖροι "comrades" instead of "Achaeans." Kept as "well-greaved" regardless of the noun.
- **κάρη κομόωντας** (already fixed as "the long-haired-of-head Achaeans") is applied at 408 to ἑταίρους "comrades." Kept as "the long-haired-of-head" / "the long-haired" regardless of the noun.
- **θεῖος** (already fixed as "divine," established in odyssey-004 for Phemius the minstrel) is applied at 394 to Ὀδυσσῆος θείοιο, "divine Odysseus." Kept as "divine," distinct from δῖος "heavenly" and ἀντίθεος "godlike," both already fixed for Odysseus elsewhere.
- **βῆ ῥ’ ἰέναι** (394) is a variant of the already-fixed "set out to go" formula (elsewhere βῆ δ’/βῆ ῥ’ ἴμεν, with the older infinitive ἴμεν rather than ἰέναι, both from εἶμι). No new row: the rendering "set out to go / set out for..." already covers it.

## An inherited discrepancy, flagged rather than silently fixed

Line 345–347 of this part (Εὐρύκλει’, Ὦπος θυγάτηρ Πεισηνορίδαο) is word-for-word identical to a line already published in odyssey-004 (1.428), whose shipped `l` reads "...Peisenor's grandson." Strictly, Πεισηνορίδαο "son of Peisenor" agrees with Ὦψ, so the sense is that Ops was Peisenor's son and Eurycleia his *granddaughter*, not "grandson." The repeated-line rule requires this part to reuse the shipped `l` verbatim, so the discrepancy is carried over rather than corrected here (the shipped `i` for the same line already reads correctly, "daughter of Ops son of Peisenor," and this part's `i` follows that). Flagged here for the owner/reviewer, since odyssey-008 cannot correct an already-published unit from odyssey-004; the note at 2.345 in this part's `units.json` also states the discrepancy in place.
